mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 2% over the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND RSAFS > 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when both PAYEMS and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4% combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a hardening labor market downturn, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% AND PAYEMS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
